title: What not-all-equal forces
claim: For a knot pattern under NAE with a state: L1 nothing is frozen, every tied pair is equal or unequal, every hollow triple misses exactly one complementary pair (a plain or signed NAE); L2 a Pasch forces NAE on its four complementary triples (same 18 states as the octahedron); L3 a book of any number of pages, as the whole pattern, is read faithfully; L4 the cut weighted by knots per pair is at most twice the knots, with equality exactly at states, so lambda-fold pair counts give states cutting two thirds of the co-knotted pairs and 2-(v,3,lambda) designs (lambda >= 1) have no state for v >= 5; L5 patterns with the same knot count on every pair have the same states, so at most one of them is read faithfully.
failure_conditions: A base with an NAE emergent knot forbidding other than one complementary pair, or a frozen distinction.
A Pasch whose complementary triple is not forced.
A book that is not read faithfully.
A base whose weighted cut exceeds twice its knots, or equals it at a non-state.
foundation_claim_scope: Finite bases of three-place knots under NAE, with any number of knots per pair; no source label needed.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the owner's go-ahead on 2026-11-11; read by an independent referee (a fresh Claude agent with its own code), which found L1 to L4 proved with wording fixes (made) and suggested L5.
validation.status: proved by hand; check.py C1 to C7 passed (result.json); refereed
validation.novelty: known (L1: the co-clone IN2 of complement-closed relations; L4: the NAE-to-max-cut triangle gadget and Rosa's counting) and known-with-delta (L2, L5: elementary consequences with trades; L3 elementary); the reading of what NAE forces on unnamed triples is the delta.
